notes: Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production inference (customer-facing chat + internal reranking pipelines).
Primary ask: deterministic throughput + P99 latency guarantees for peak trading-hours chat (low-latency) and nightly high-volume embeddings (cost-efficiency).
Workload split: ~60% real-time chat (interactive), 30% reranking for fraud scoring, 10% batch embeddings (offline).
Latency targets: chat P95 < 120ms, P99 < 250ms for 512-token average response; reranking P95 < 200ms; embeddings batch throughput target 200k vectors/day with cost cap.
Baseline metrics provided by customer (initial telemetry):

- Avg incoming QPS baseline: 85 qps (UTC 14:00-18:00), peak observed 220 qps (10-minute spike during market open), median response token length ~120 tokens, avg output tokens/sec per request ~60 tokens/sec.
- Reranking job: 120 qps during peak micro-bursts, typical candidate list sizes 20-50, service needs p99 latency < 200ms for top-k scoring to keep downstream SLA.
- Batch embeddings window: nightly 3am-6am, target throughput 200k items in 3 hours => ~18.5 qps sustained but heavy tokenization and IO overheads.
Capacity planning assumptions discussed in call:
- Model selection: prefer Llama-2.2B or similar quantized FP16 variant for chat baseline; planning for fallback to a 7B variant under burst to preserve latency SLOs.
- Per-GPU throughput estimates (preliminary): 40-50 qps for 2.2B at 512 tokens (latency budget 120-200ms) on A100 equivalent; 7B yields higher per-GPU qps but different quality/cost tradeoff.
- KV-cache and continuous batching can reduce effective per-token compute by ~18% on observed prompt reuse pattern — Redwood Optimize recommendation noted.
Workshop objective (agreed): run Dedicated capacity sizing workshop with infra + ML leads to produce a 'Reserved GPU Plan' covering steady-state and burst windows, and SLA negotiation points.
Key SLA asks from Sentinel (they want in term sheet):
- Guaranteed 99th percentile latency numbers for the reserved capacity during agreed peak windows (with credits for misses),
- Predictable throughput floor (baseline QPS) with documented burst absorb behavior,
- Clear fallback model routing rules and performance profiles included in the SLA,
- Enhanced audit logging and weekly utilization reports for cost chargebacks.

Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-18): 'We need to be able to forecast cost within 5% and never drop below P99 SLOs during open-market trading windows. If your Dedicated plan can't guarantee that, we need to see fallback behavior that preserves business continuity.'
Action items captured:
- Redwood to run microbenchmark guide on their representative prompts and return token/sec and latency per model variant (by 2026-02-24).
- Scheduling 2-hr on-site/remote sizing workshop with infra (network/VPC) and ML_engine teams: target 2026-03-04.
- Customer to provide sanitized sample prompt set (500 requests) and traffic histogram (requested 2026-02-20).
- AE to draft initial term sheet with SLA targets and credits (in progress).
Technical notes from discovery call:
- Network egress constraints: firewalls and strict egress rules; will require Private control plane + VPC peering for Dedicated. Potential on-prem for highest isolation in pilot cluster.
- Storage/embedding persistence: prefer in-region object storage with AES-KMS; need integration details for KMS key rotation (security asks).
- Burst capacity: want 2x baseline for 30-minute windows during market events; discuss soft vs hard burst billing model (crediting vs on-demand premiums).
- Autoscaling policy preference: reserved baseline + predictable scheduled scale-up for known market windows, with manual override and canary fallback routing to smaller model variants.
Procurement & legal notes:
- Procurement timeline: internal budget committee meets 2026-03-15, legal requires SOC2 + addendum for data residency and incident response timelines.
- Pricing sensitivity: prefer yearly reserved capacity commitment with quarterly review — open to pilot month-to-month ahead of commit (pilot ARR < $100k).
Risks flagged by AE:

- If benchmarked per-GPU throughput falls 20% lower than Redwood's initial estimate, baseline reserved units will not meet P99 SLOs; must plan fallback routing to 7B variant and increase burst reserve.
- Network/VPC setup timeline could push go-live by 4-6 weeks if security team's questions are not resolved before procurement.
Next internal Redwood prep before workshop:
- Prepare model perf matrix: qps / tokens/sec / p95/p99 latency for candidate models (2.2B fp16, 2.2B int8, 7B fp16) on target hw profiles.
- Draft reserved GPU sizing scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive — include cost delta and fallback routing plan.
- Bring sample term sheet language for SLA p99 guarantees, remediation credits, and scheduled maintenance windows.
Customer sentiment: engaged, pragmatic; procurement timeline aggressive but will test pilot if workshop shows predictable economics.
